title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 211 (Agent’s duty in conducting principal’s business)

content.overview: An agent is bound to conduct the business of his principal according to the directions given by the principal, or, in the absence of any such directions, according to the custom which prevails in doing business of the same kind at the place where the agent conducts such business. When the agent acts otherwise, if any loss be sustained, he must make it good to his principal, and if any profit accrues, he must account for it.
content.glance: Follow principal’s directions or local custom of similar business; make good loss and account for profit if acting otherwise.

sections.heading: Directions or custom
sections.body: Conduct business according to principal’s directions, or absent directions according to local custom of similar business.

sections.heading: Consequences of acting otherwise
sections.body: Make good any loss sustained; account for any profit that accrues.

provisions.title: Agent’s duty in conducting principal’s business

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 211 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Identify directions or applicable custom; test departure; apply make-good loss and account-for-profit consequences.

examTips: Directions first; then custom of similar business at the place.
